description: The technologies EAOS knows how to lay out, by concern, for building a project from a plan (eaos/blueprint.py). Each concern has a recommended option and alternatives. Every option lives behind one adapter folder (its port): only that folder may import the option's packages, which eaos/blueprint.py checks after every build card, so changing an option later is replacing one folder. `switch` says, in plain words, what changing to that option involves.

react-vite.name: React with Vite
react-vite.why: The most used way to build web screens; fast, simple, and every AI assistant knows it well.
react-vite.switch: Screens live in web/src; another framework replaces that folder, the server stays as it is.

next.name: Next.js
next.why: Screens and server in one project, with pages rendered on the server for search engines.
next.switch: A bigger move: Next.js also hosts the server routes, so the api concern changes with it.

hono.name: Hono
hono.why: Small, fast and typed; runs on Node and on edge platforms alike.
hono.switch: Routes live in server/src/interface/http; another framework replaces that folder only.

express.name: Express
express.why: The oldest and most known Node server; the most examples online.
express.switch: Routes live in server/src/interface/http; another framework replaces that folder only.

fastify.name: Fastify
fastify.why: Fast, with schemas for every request built in.
fastify.switch: Routes live in server/src/interface/http; another framework replaces that folder only.

none.name: No server of our own
none.why: A site with no private data, or a hosted back end (Supabase) that the screens call directly.
none.switch: Adding a server later adds the server/ folder; the screens keep calling the same client module.

postgres-drizzle.name: PostgreSQL with Drizzle
postgres-drizzle.why: PostgreSQL is the most trusted open database; Drizzle keeps the tables as typed code, with migrations.
postgres-drizzle.switch: Only server/src/infrastructure/database uses it; another database replaces that folder, the rest calls the same repositories.

supabase.name: Supabase (hosted PostgreSQL with sign-in and storage)
supabase.why: A hosted database, sign-in and file storage in one service; the least to run yourself.
supabase.switch: Only the database (and, if chosen, auth) adapter folder uses it; moving to your own PostgreSQL replaces that folder.

prisma-postgres.name: PostgreSQL with Prisma
prisma-postgres.why: A widely used typed database layer with a visual schema.
prisma-postgres.switch: Only server/src/infrastructure/database uses it; another database layer replaces that folder.

sqlite-drizzle.name: SQLite with Drizzle
sqlite-drizzle.why: One file, no server: good for a small app or a first version.
sqlite-drizzle.switch: Drizzle speaks PostgreSQL too: moving is changing the driver in the database folder and running the migrations.

none.name: No database
none.why: The app keeps no data of its own.
none.switch: Adding a database later adds its adapter folder; nothing else is rewritten.

better-auth.name: Better Auth
better-auth.why: Open-source sign-in kept in your own database: e-mail, social sign-in, sessions.
better-auth.switch: Only server/src/infrastructure/auth uses it; the rest asks one function who the user is.

supabase-auth.name: Supabase Auth
supabase-auth.why: Sign-in from Supabase, natural when the data is there too.
supabase-auth.switch: Only the auth adapter folder uses it; the rest asks one function who the user is.

clerk.name: Clerk
clerk.why: Hosted sign-in with ready screens; the least to build.
clerk.switch: Only the auth adapter folders use it; the rest asks one function who the user is.

none.name: No sign-in
none.why: Everyone sees the same thing; nothing is private.
none.switch: Adding sign-in later adds the auth adapter; routes ask the same function who the user is.

tailwind.name: Tailwind CSS
tailwind.why: One consistent design vocabulary; the style sits next to the screen it styles.
tailwind.switch: Shared looks live in web/src/ui; a new style system replaces those components first.

css-modules.name: Plain CSS modules
css-modules.why: No extra tool: each screen has its own CSS file.
css-modules.switch: Shared looks live in web/src/ui; a new style system replaces those components first.

vitest-playwright.name: Vitest for the logic, Playwright for the screens
vitest-playwright.why: Fast tests for every rule, and real browser tests for every user flow.
vitest-playwright.switch: Tests are plain files next to what they test; another runner reads them with small changes.

always.language: TypeScript, strict: the types catch mistakes before anything runs, and every AI assistant writes it well.
